headline: mat-surface-adsorption: adsorption energies on the sites of a slab
claim: An AtomisticSkills skill that cuts a slab from a bulk crystal, places an adsorbate on every ontop, bridge and hollow site and relaxes each with a machine-learned potential.

hero.title: E(adslab) - E(slab) - E(adsorbate)
hero.text: AdsorptionCalc relaxes the bulk, cuts the slab at the given Miller index, relaxes the clean slab and the gas-phase molecule, then relaxes the adsorbate on each site. Each site's adsorption energy is the difference in eV.

features.title: Catalysis-trained potentials
features.text: Models trained on Open Catalyst data come first: EquiformerV2 S2EF-OC20, UMA uma-s-1p1 and MACE-OMAT-0. MPtrj-only models are discouraged for their force errors.

features.title: Slab geometry
features.text: The slab is at least 10 A thick and the vacuum at least 20 A by default. The adsorbate starts 0.9 A above the surface. --adsorption_sites picks ontop, bridge or hollow.

features.title: Relaxations
features.text: By default ASE BFGS relaxes the bulk, the clean slab and the adsorbate to fmax 0.05 eV/A within 500 steps. Each of the three relaxations has a flag to switch it off.

features.title: Inputs and outputs
features.text: Inputs are a bulk CIF or POSCAR, an adsorbate XYZ or SMILES string and a Miller index such as [1,1,1]. adsorption_results.json lists every site and the most stable one.

default force convergence of the relaxations

workflow.title: Pick model and facet
workflow.text: Choose an OC-trained model and a Miller index. Supply the bulk and adsorbate files.

workflow.title: Build the slab
workflow.text: calculate_adsorption.py relaxes the bulk and cuts a slab, 10 A of material, 20 A vacuum.

workflow.title: Place and relax
workflow.text: The adsorbate is set 0.9 A above each ontop, bridge and hollow site and relaxed.

workflow.title: Read the energies
workflow.text: adsorption_results.json gives E_ads per site and names the most stable site.

applications.title: CO on Cu(111)
applications.text: The worked example relaxes CO on the ontop, bridge and hollow sites of a Cu(111) slab with MACE-OMAT-0-small. The README gives -0.5 to -1.5 eV as typical, ontop usually most stable.

detail.heading: One site at a time on a relaxed slab
detail.text: The skill wraps matcalc's AdsorptionCalc and its calc_adslabs call. It relaxes the bulk, cuts a slab for the requested Miller index given as a JSON list such as [1,1,1], and relaxes the clean slab and the isolated adsorbate on their own. AdsorptionCalc then places the adsorbate on each ontop, bridge and hollow site, 0.9 A above the surface by default, and relaxes every adsorbate-slab configuration. The adsorption energy of a site is E(adsorbate+slab) - E(slab) - E(adsorbate). A negative value is exothermic, and the SKILL.md gives -0.5 to -5.0 eV as the usual range for strong chemisorption.

detail.heading: Numerics and cost
detail.text: The relaxations use ASE's BFGS to fmax 0.05 eV/A with at most 500 steps. The slab holds at least 10 A of material and 20 A of vacuum, which the SKILL.md calls critical against periodic-image interactions, and layered materials may need a thicker slab. Cost scales with the number of sites and the slab size, so --adsorption_sites ontop or bridge trims the search. The bulk should be a well-relaxed crystal and the adsorbate a gas-phase molecule, not a periodic structure.

detail.heading: Potentials and environment
detail.text: The SKILL.md ranks potentials for this task. Open Catalyst models are first: FAIRChem EquiformerV2-31M and 153M S2EF-OC20-All+MD, UMA uma-s-1p1 and uma-m-1p1, and MACE-OMAT-0-small and medium. MatPES models such as CHGNet-PES-MatPES-PBE-1M-2026.9 and TensorNet-PES-MatPES-PBE-2025.2 come second. It advises against models trained only on MPtrj because of their force errors. The command runs through venv/run in the fairchem environment for FairChem models and in mlip for MACE and MatGL. The sibling skill mat-surface-energy computes surface energies and Wulff shapes.
